chains.title: GABPA binds the alt allele more strongly and promotes TERT expression
chains.element: Promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 containing the variant

links.claim: GABPA has its own QBiC-SELEX model and is a passing member in the ETS group with alt-more binding (z 68.47, effect 4.01 alt more; group G003 passing models have the alt-more sign). GABPA is chosen over other ETS factors because E18b directly reports that the C228T mutation recruited GA-binding protein and engendered low-level TERT expression; E17 adds that GABPA ChIP peaks contain this variant in HepG2 and SK-N-SH, though no glioblastoma GABPA peak is reported and absence there is ambiguous.
The variant lies in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 at the TERT promoter.
TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene, 0.0 kb from its TSS, and the variant is annotated as an upstream TERT promoter variant.
The relevant expression context is glioblastoma, and TERT promoter mutations are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma.

E18b directly supports that the C228T mutation recruits GABP and engenders low-level TERT expression, consistent with a GABPA-mediated increase in TERT/telomerase in tumors; E18a and E04a support TERT promoter mutations as a cause of TERT activation. E18d cautions that pooled screens did not detect a TERT or ETS-factor dependency, so the functional magnitude and necessity of GABPA remain uncertain.

predictions: GABPA ChIP is stronger on the alt allele at chr5:1295113 in heterozygous glioblastoma cells.
Allele-resolved TERT expression is higher from the alt allele.
GABPA depletion reduces TERT expression preferentially in alt-allele glioblastoma cells.

GABPA depletion does not reduce TERT expression in glioblastoma cells carrying the alt allele.
Allele-resolved TERT expression does not show the alt allele higher in heterozygous glioblastoma cells.

chains.title: ETS1 binds the alt allele more strongly and activates TERT
chains.element: Promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 containing the variant

links.claim: ETS1 is named as an own-model-covered ETS factor in E06 at 61.01 TPM in the glioblastoma expression context, but E06 does not explicitly enumerate ETS1 among the passing members or give an ETS1-specific z-score/effect sign. The alt-more direction is therefore extrapolated from the group G003 alt-more sign and remains weak until ETS1-specific QBiC-SELEX detail is checked.
The variant lies in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 at the TERT promoter.
TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene, 0.0 kb from its TSS, and the variant is annotated as an upstream TERT promoter variant.
The relevant expression context is glioblastoma, and TERT promoter mutations are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma.

If ETS1 were the functional ETS factor, stronger alt-allele binding would increase TERT expression. However, E18d explicitly reports that pooled screens did not detect dependency on an ETS factor known to activate TPMs, so this chain is disfavored relative to GABPA.

predictions: ETS1-specific binding is stronger on the alt allele at chr5:1295113.
ETS1 depletion reduces TERT expression in glioblastoma cells carrying the alt allele.
The allele-specific effect is not explained by GABPA.
falsified_if: ETS1-specific QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific ETS1 ChIP does not show alt > ref at this base.
ETS1 knockdown does not affect TERT expression in the relevant glioblastoma context.
GABPA accounts for all allele-specific ETS-family binding at this promoter.

chains.title: TFAP2A binds the ref allele more strongly and may repress TERT
chains.element: Promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 containing the variant

links.claim: TFAP2A has its own QBiC-SELEX model in the AP-2 group and is a passing member with z -28.06; the group's passing models have the alt-less sign, so TFAP2A is predicted to bind the ref allele more strongly. This is an in vitro binding prediction only.
The variant lies in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 at the TERT promoter.
TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene, 0.0 kb from its TSS, and the variant is annotated as an upstream TERT promoter variant.
The relevant expression context is glioblastoma, and TERT promoter mutations are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma.

No supplied evidence shows that TFAP2A represses TERT. If TFAP2A were a repressor, loss of its ref-allele binding on the alt allele would derepress TERT and increase telomerase activity, but this remains speculative.

predictions: TFAP2A ChIP is stronger on the ref allele at chr5:1295113.
TFAP2A depletion increases TERT expression in the relevant cells.
The alt allele increases TERT expression by losing a repressive AP-2 site.
falsified_if: TFAP2A ChIP does not show ref > alt at this promoter.
TFAP2A is not a repressor of TERT in the relevant cell context.
Loss of TFAP2A binding on the alt allele does not increase TERT expression.

grades_v0.reason: E06 directly lists GABPA as an own-model passing member with z 68.47 and the group's passing models have the alt-more sign, so the QBiC-SELEX direction is consistent. But this is an in vitro binding prediction only; there is no allele-specific ChIP or perturbation evidence for GABPA at this variant. The choice of GABPA within the ETS group is also under-justified: ETV5 is the best model, ETS1 is higher expressed, and many ETS factors pass.

E03 places the variant inside promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530, and E01 annotates an ENSR5_832QG promoter feature. This directly supports the element claim, although E03 z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific.
E02 reports TERT as the nearest protein-coding gene at 0.0 kb from its TSS, and E01 annotates the variant as an upstream TERT variant. This supports TERT as the linked gene.

E05 states the expression context is DepMap subtype median glioblastoma, and E04d/E04g/E04h quote literature that TERT promoter mutations are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. This supports glioblastoma as a relevant context, though the QBiC-SELEX screen itself is not cell-type evidence.

E04a supports that TERT promoter mutations are a major cause of telomerase activation in melanoma, and E04d/E04g/E04h support frequency in glioblastoma. None of these citations show that GABPA binding at this promoter increases TERT expression or telomerase activity. The TF-specific mechanistic part of the phenotype claim is unsupported and over-claims from QBiC-SELEX binding to disease mechanism.

E06 shows ETS1 has an own model and is in the group TFs-covered list at 61.01 TPM, but it does not explicitly list ETS1 among the enumerated passing members or give an ETS1-specific z-score/effect sign. The claim extrapolates from the group's alt-more sign to ETS1. QBiC-SELEX is in vitro binding only, so this is at best weak and needs qbic_tf_detail(ETS1) confirmation.
E03 places the variant inside promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530, and E01 supports a TERT promoter feature. This directly supports the element claim.
E02 reports TERT at 0.0 kb from its TSS and E01 annotates the variant as upstream of TERT. This supports TERT as the target gene.
E05 gives the glioblastoma expression context, and E04d/E04g/E04h support the relevance of TERT promoter mutations in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. This is adequate for the cell-type link.

The phenotype link is explicitly conditional and cites only general TERT promoter mutation/telomerase literature (E04a, E04d, E04g, E04h). No citation shows ETS1 binding at this element, ETS1-mediated TERT activation, or an allele-specific effect. This is a speculative alternative, not evidence-supported.

E09 directly lists TFAP2A as a passing AP-2-group member with z -28.06 and the group's alt-less sign, so the ref-more direction is internally consistent. But this is still only a QBiC-SELEX in vitro binding prediction, with no allele-specific occupancy or perturbation evidence; at best weak for the binding link.
E03 supports the variant being in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530, and E01 supports a TERT promoter feature. This directly supports the element claim.
E02 reports TERT as the nearest protein-coding gene at 0.0 kb from its TSS, and E01 annotates an upstream TERT variant. This supports the gene link.

E05 provides the glioblastoma expression context and E04d/E04g/E04h support TERT promoter mutation relevance in glioblastoma. This supports the cell-type link, though not TFAP2A-specific activity in glioblastoma.

The claim requires TFAP2A to repress TERT and loss of TFAP2A binding on the alt allele to derepress TERT. E04a only states that TERT promoter mutations generally cause telomerase activation in melanoma; it provides no evidence for TFAP2A repression of TERT. The chain itself admits this is not established.

grades_final.reason: E16 gives a GABPA-specific own QBiC-SELEX model that passes the gate with alt-more binding (z 68.47, effect 4.01), and E06 places GABPA in the passing ETS group with the same sign. E18b directly reports that the C228T mutation recruited GA-binding protein, which is stronger than a QBiC prediction alone. E17 supports GABPA ChIP occupancy containing the variant in HepG2 and SK-N-SH, but not in glioblastoma and not allele-specifically.

The claim appropriately notes E18d, which reports no detected dependency on TERT or a known ETS factor in pooled screens, so the functional magnitude/necessity remains uncertain but the link itself is not unsupported.

E06 lists ETS1 as an own-model-covered ETS factor at 61.01 TPM, but does not explicitly enumerate ETS1 among the passing members or provide an ETS1-specific z-score/effect sign. The alt-more direction is extrapolated from the group G003 sign. An ETS1-specific qbic_tf_detail lookup should be used to confirm passing status and direction.

next_experiment: Allele-resolved TERT expression by RNA-seq or RT-PCR in glioblastoma cells heterozygous for C228T, using phased heterozygous SNPs to assign TERT reads to ref versus alt alleles. It is the cheapest because it uses RNA rather than ChIP or perturbation and directly separates H1_GABPA from H4_null: H1 predicts higher TERT expression from the alt allele, whereas H4 predicts no allelic difference. It does not by itself prove GABPA, so a positive result would then require allele-specific GABPA ChIP.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.
Understanding both telomere-dependent and -independent TERT functions is essential for developing effective biomarkers and therapies that overcome resistance and slow melanoma progression.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
Mutations in the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter region (TPM), particularly C228T and C250T, are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM).

The rs2853669 C allele may increase GBM susceptibility and, when in cis with TPM, is associated with reduced TERT expression and poorer prognosis, underscoring its biological and clinical significance in TPM-mutant GBM.
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.
Among 112 patients, 70 (62.5%) harbored TERTp mutations.

Groups shown: 10; dropped because no TF in the group reaches 1 TPM: 47 (Ets, 3 models z 16.96, Myb/SANT, 1 model z -16.15, Homeodomain, 1 model z -15.52, bHLH, 1 model z -14.2, bHLH, 1 model z -14.2). Passing groups ranked below the ones shown: 173. In the group rows, 'own model' means the TF has its own QBiC-SELEX model and 'mapped' that it is covered only through CIS-BP-mapped models of related TFs. A TF not named in any group row may still have its own model, even one that passes the gate: look it up with qbic_tf_detail before stating its coverage or a QBiC-SELEX direction for it. predicted_effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only: expression and chromatin decide whether a change matters.

Heterozygous TERT (telomerase reverse transcriptase) promoter mutations (TPMs) facilitate TERT expression and are the most frequent mutation in glioblastoma (GBM).

However, the mutation recruited GA-Binding Protein and engendered low-level TERT expression resulting in enhanced tumorigenesis and maintenance of short telomeres upon secondary passage as observed in human GBM.
Here we used pooled CRISPR/Cas9-based approaches to identify vulnerabilities associated with telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations (TPMs) found in >80% of glioblastomas.
However, we could not detect dependencies on either TERT itself or on an E-twenty six transcription (ETS) factor known to activate TPMs.

Point mutations in the core promoter region of the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) gene have been found to occur at high frequencies in several tumour types and considered a primary cause of telomerase reactivation in cancer cells.

These mutations promote TERT gene expression by multiple mechanisms, including the generation of novel binding sites for nuclear transcription factors, displacement of negative regulators from DNA G-quadruplexes, recruitment of epigenetic activators and disruption of long-range interactions between TERT locus and telomeres.
